executionPlan: Read-only audit in the isolated worktree on Node 22. Ran npm run lint and npm run build. Parsed the glTF JSON chunk and accessor binaries of avatar.glb, walk.glb, run.glb (plus durations of the other 7 clips) with scratch Node scripts kept outside the repo. Compared rest rotations of avatar and Mixamo clips. Collected npm view peer-dependency evidence. Downloaded (npm pack to scratch, no install) the rapier3d-compat and @react-three/rapier tarballs to measure the WASM payload. Removed the .next and next-env.d.ts build artifacts afterwards because the repo has no .gitignore.
summary: Build passes (exit 0) but npm run lint is not a working gate: no .eslintrc exists, so next lint opens an interactive setup prompt and exits 0 without linting, and the existing eslint.config.mjs fails under ESLint 8.57 (next/typescript missing). The avatar is a standard Mixamo-named 54-joint Avaturn skeleton with correct Hips/Spine/Neck/Head/foot joints, so reuse is supported. walk.glb and run.glb are real distinct clips whose files are about 98% redundant Mixamo mesh data. A locomotion retarget should drop Hips rotation and translation (Hips rest rotation differs by 89.4 deg), keep quaternion tracks for existing joints, and consider rest-delta correction for feet, neck and arms. Recommend @react-three/rapier@1.5.0 (peer ranges satisfied; WASM about 1.44 MB raw, 765 KB gzip) and Vitest for unit tests.

retargeting.assessment: Quaternion-only is sound: Mixamo translation tracks are in centimetres and scale tracks are all 1.0 (no information). Hips exclusion is necessary for rotation because Mixamo Hips carries a baked -90 deg X rest rotation (89.4 deg off the avatar) and, for run, a 36 deg yaw drift. Existing approach copies absolute local quaternions rather than rest-relative deltas, which is tolerable where rest rotations match (legs under 2 deg) but leaves about 12 deg error on feet/toes and 18-26 deg on arms/neck.

keep: Quaternion tracks for Spine, Spine1, Spine2, Neck, Head, both Shoulder/Arm/ForeArm/Hand, finger 1-3 joints, UpLeg, Leg, Foot, ToeBase (locomotion legs and counter-swing arms are the point of the clip)
dropOrHandleSeparately: Hips quaternion (rest-frame mismatch, run yaw drift)
Hips translation entirely, as root motion: the character controller owns world position and speed
All scale tracks and non-Hips translation tracks (Mixamo cm units)
Tracks targeting nodes absent from the avatar (HeadTop_End, finger 4 joints, Toe_End) to avoid console warnings; filter by skin joint names
Optionally keep only the vertical (up-axis) Hips bob, scaled by avatar hip height / Mixamo hip height (about 0.984 / about 1.0), if the pelvis looks stiff; verify visually
adjust: Apply rest-pose delta correction (avatarRest * inverse(mixamoRest) * clipQuat) for feet, toes, neck, head, shoulders and arms, or accept the 12-18 deg offset after a visual check; requires a browser to validate
Trim the duplicated last frame (AnimationUtils.subclip to frames-1) so looping has no 1-frame hold
Strip the avatar's embedded idle Hips translation (or crossfade carefully) because locomotion clips drop Hips translation and a crossfade would otherwise blend a moving Hips with a fixed one
Set clip timeScale = controllerSpeed / clipSpeed (walk about 0.99 m/s, run about 2.3 m/s forward) to limit foot sliding; scale for avatar height 1.865 m vs Beta 1.809 m (about 1.03)
recommendation.existingGestureCode: Keep GestureClips loading and retargetClip behaviour for the talking hero unchanged; add a separate locomotion retarget helper in the game module rather than editing the hero path.

avatarDecision.decision: REUSE public/avatar.glb and the existing walk/run clips; no rebuild
evidence: Skeleton uses standard Mixamo-compatible joint names (Hips root, Spine/Spine1/Spine2, Neck, Head, Left/Right UpLeg/Leg/Foot/ToeBase), 52 of 54 joints retarget by name
Rest-pose differences are small for legs (under 2 deg) and moderate for feet (about 12 deg); no missing joints that locomotion needs
Both T-pose, similar height (1.865 m vs 1.809 m)
Triangle count 21090 and 31 textures (3.9 MB) are acceptable for a single hero character, but the 14 MB file size is the main budget risk
conditions: Visual check in a browser for foot pitch and arm swing after retarget (not possible here)
Because the 14 MB avatar is already loaded by the hero, the game must reuse the same loaded asset (useGLTF cache) and add no second copy to the 8 MB additional budget
Optional later: texture or morph-target compression of avatar.glb is out of scope unless performance gaps show a problem

assetGaps.existingClips: wave, run, walk, dance, silly_dance, zombie, defeated, dodge, climb (9 clips, about 1.86-2.0 MB each because each embeds the redundant Mixamo mesh)
missing: idle (a locomotion-quality idle; the avatar's embedded 8 s avaturn_animation can serve initially but carries Hips translation and morph weights)
celebration (existing dance/silly_dance 3.9-5.2 s can be used as an interim celebration)
assetGaps.recommendedSourcing: Download the missing clips from Mixamo (Adobe account, 'Without Skin', 30 fps, FBX/GLB via a converter) in the same Beta rig so they pass through the same retarget, e.g. Idle, Jump, Falling Idle, Hard Landing, Victory/Dance; strip mesh and skin to cut each clip to about 25-40 KB. Alternative: author in Blender on the avatar skeleton.
assetGaps.licenseRequirements: Record for every new asset: source URL, Adobe ID used, download date, clip name, and the Mixamo terms in force (Mixamo animations are free for personal, commercial and non-profit use but must not be redistributed as standalone asset packs; verify current terms before use). No license record currently exists for avatar.glb (Avaturn) or the 9 existing Mixamo clips; add an ASSETS or license note when new assets are added (constraint: no third-party assets without a recorded source and license).
assetGaps.budgetNote: Stripped clips are tiny (about 25-40 KB), so five new clips plus 2 stripped existing ones fit easily within the 8 MB additional-asset budget alongside the about 0.77 MB gzip physics bundle.
